The man who coined the term. Musician Harry "The Hipster" Gibson. New York, ca. 1948

Harry "The Hipster" Gibson (June 27, 1915 – May 3, 1991) was a jazz pianist, singer and songwriter.

Gibson played New York style Stride piano and boogie woogie while singing in a wild, unrestrained style and was known for writing unusual songs, which are considered ahead of their time. While working on 52nd Street ("Swing Street") at night, Gibson was a fellow at the Juilliard Graduate School during the day. At the time, Juilliard was strictly a classical music academy, which partly explains the richness of the music he brought to the jazz world and the richness he brought to classical music with his boogie woogie training. Gibson claims he coined the term hipster some time between 1939 and 1945, when he was performing on Swing Street and he started using "Harry the Hipster" as his stage name.

Here he is performing "Keep the Beat".
